title: Today in one sentence
text: Tech stocks bounced back on Monday: the Nasdaq 100 fund QQQ rose 1.2%, the S&P 500 fund SPY rose 0.4% and Amazon jumped 5.0%, but Friday's drop was bigger, so the week starts as a partial recovery; next up are Lockheed Martin's results on Thursday and the Fed meeting on October 27 and 28.

title: Chip stocks recover part of Friday's drop
text: Nvidia rose 1.4%, Broadcom 1.8%, Taiwan Semiconductor 1.8% and AMD 1.8%. After a hard fall, a partial bounce is common, but it does not tell us what comes next. These companies still sit well below their highs for the year.

title: Amazon is the biggest mover, up 5.0%
text: Amazon rose about 5% to $262.45, the largest gain on our list. We have not confirmed one single reason, so treat any explanation you read with care. On the Nasdaq, the Consumer Cyclical group, which includes online shopping, was the best sector, up 2.3%.

title: Safer-feeling areas lagged
text: Utilities on the Nasdaq fell 3.4% and real estate fell 1.7%, while Lockheed Martin slipped 0.7% and Eli Lilly fell 1.3%. When money rushes back into tech, quieter areas can fall behind for a day. That is one more reason a mix of industries can smooth the ride.

title: Lockheed reports on Thursday
text: Lockheed Martin will publish its quarterly results before the market opens on Thursday, October 22. Report days can bring big moves, up or down, because real numbers replace guesses.

title: Lesson 13: What is an earnings report?
text: Four times a year, a public company must tell everyone how much it sold and how much it earned in the last three months. That report is called an earnings report. Analysts, who are people paid to study companies, make a guess ahead of time. If the real numbers beat the guess, the stock often jumps; if they fall short, it often drops, even when the company made a lot of money. What the company says about the next few months matters too. Lockheed Martin reports this Thursday, so it is a good one to watch. This is for learning, not advice to buy or sell anything.
